bugClass.title: Schedule-off state suppresses a confirmed startup retry
bugClass.cause: A manual request is still current and the host confirms the run never started, but retry preparation treats a scheduling-off state as an unattended cancellation hold. Without an applicable manual-startup-retry override, that gate suppresses the one explicit startup retry. Related variants may use scheduleOff/schedule_off, automaticRequestHold/schedulingHold, or retireUnstartedRun/prepareRetry/confirmNeverStarted/automaticHostHold.
bugClass.criteria: Positive when a site gates a confirmed never-started explicit retry for a still-current manual request on schedule-off or an equivalent unattended hold, and no applicable manualStartupRetry or equivalent override permits it. Either schedule-off or the equivalent unattended hold can independently produce the suppression. Exclude retries after a session started, explicit token withdrawal, owner/parked/answer holds, protective routing, and policy-helper definitions without the suppressing retry path.

candidates.evidence: Lines 33–45 route `prepare` through `prepareRetry` for the current owned attempt. The excerpt does not show whether the run was confirmed never started, whether schedule-off suppresses the retry, or whether a manual-startup override applies.
`trackerLegacyExitReceipt.ts` lines 17–32 detects legacy startup evidence and calls `confirmNeverStarted`; the excerpt shows confirmation only, with no retry preparation or scheduling-off gate.

`trackerDispatchObservations.ts` lines 29–41 emits a `never-started` event only for queued runs past the startup grace period when the runner confirms. It does not show how the resulting retry is prepared or gated.

`launchEligibility.ts` lines 110–128 defines `automaticRequestHold` as a scheduling and launcher-enabled policy helper. This excerpt does not show a confirmed never-started retry path using it, so it cannot establish the candidate cause.

`runTransition.ts` lines 19–31 routes a `never-started` event to `retireUnstartedRun`, but the excerpt does not show whether that path retries a still-current manual request or applies a scheduling-off hold.

In `runClaim.ts` lines 48–62, `prepareRetry` clears `scheduleOff` before calling `schedulingHold` whenever `run.manualStartupRetry` is true. Thus schedule-off does not suppress this explicit startup retry; other holds may still apply.

`trackerHostRunner.ts` lines 178–196 clears `schedule_off` when `run.manualStartupRetry` is true before checking the stored scheduling hold. Schedule-off therefore does not suppress this explicit retry at this site.

`trackerDispatchQueue.ts` lines 34–48 explicitly skips the scheduling and automatic-permission checks when `run.manualStartupRetry` is true, then calls `prepareQueuedRun`. This visible gate does not suppress the explicit retry for schedule-off.

`runGiveUp.ts` lines 8–21 uses `schedulingHold` with `scheduleOff` cleared for manual startup; the non-manual branch uses `automaticRequestHold`. The excerpt shows an override for the relevant manual-startup path, not the reported suppression.

Lines 40–52 define `holdWithoutRunner`, which checks `schedulingHold` and scheduler pause/disabled state for due-preview reporting. This excerpt has no confirmed never-started run, retry preparation, or manual request path.
Lines 140–152 apply `automaticRequestHold` while previewing due launches. The trigger is a due-preview request; there is no confirmed startup retry or still-current manual request in this path.

Lines 18–30 apply `automaticRequestHold` in `recoveryIntent`, then queue a recovery launch only if it passes. This is a recovery-launch path, not evidence of suppressing the explicit startup retry described by the candidate class.

Lines 166–178 set `manualStartupRetry` on a retry after a startup failure when a retry choice exists. That is a visible override mechanism, and the excerpt does not show schedule-off suppressing this retry.
Lines 30–42 declare the optional `manualStartupRetry` field and describe it as continuing an explicitly requested launch that never started. This is a type definition, not a suppressing retry path.

Lines 70–82 require `automaticRequestHold` to be clear before considering an answered blocked run for resume. The trigger is an answered blocked run, which the criteria exclude; no never-started startup retry suppression is shown.
Lines 12–24 reject delegation when `automaticRequestHold` applies. The trigger is a due-launch delegation request; the excerpt does not show a confirmed never-started explicit retry.
